title: Sacrifices for ignorance and unwillingness
english: Concerning sacrifices for ignorance and for what is not voluntary. The high priest also offers for his own ignorance. The law is merciful: ignorance is not absolute innocence.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is explaining the Levitical sacrifices for sins committed in ignorance or without deliberate will, and notes that even the high priest must offer for his own ignorance.

title: The guilt of silent witnesses
english: If a soul has heard the voice of an oath and is a witness and has not reported it, it will receive sin (Leviticus 5:1). The silence of those who know is guilt. Truth is in the mouth of the church.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is explaining the sin-offering for a soul that hears a public oath and, though a witness, does not speak up.

title: Contact with death makes unclean
english: A soul that has touched a dead body or something captured by a wild beast is unclean (Leviticus 5:2). Dead conduct brings uncleanness. Separate the holy from the unclean (Leviticus 10:10).
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is applying the Levitical purity rules to the soul, explaining that contact with what is dead or captured by a wild beast makes one unclean.

title: Oaths bind the speaker
english: If someone has sworn to do evil or good and has hidden it, he has sinned (Leviticus 5:4). A rash word becomes a bond. Let your speech be yes yes, no no (Matthew 5:37).
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is explaining Leviticus 5:4, where a rash oath to do evil or good, once hidden, makes a person guilty.

title: Confession precedes the offering
english: He will confess his sin and offer a female from the flock (Leviticus 5:6). Confession comes before the sacrifice. Christ is the lamb; the penitent soul is the sheep.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is explaining the order of the sin offering: confession of sin comes before the gift, and the female animal from the flock signifies Christ as lamb and the penitent soul as sheep.

title: God adjusts the burden and accepts the poor's gifts
english: If his hand does not reach to a sheep, two turtledoves. God tempers burdens. He does not scorn the gifts of the poor.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is commenting on Leviticus 5:7, where the law allows a poor person to offer two turtledoves instead of a sheep for a sin offering.

title: The poor person's sin offering without oil or incense
english: If he cannot bring even birds, then fine flour without oil and frankincense, because it is a sacrifice for sin (Leviticus 5:11). Mourning, not a feast. The rough bread of repentance.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is explaining the graduated sin offerings in Leviticus, now reaching the very poorest offering of fine flour without oil or frankincense.

title: Restitution with increase for sins against holy things
english: If someone has sinned against the holy things of the Lord, he shall add a fifth part (Leviticus 5:16). Restitution with increase. Grace does not nourish fraud. Amen.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
Ephesians 4:28 dropped 2026-09-17 triage (A13): Restitution text; no labor/sharing hook for Eph 4:28.
orientation: Origen is explaining the Levitical rule that one who sins against the Lord's holy things must make restitution plus a fifth.
